The FOMC statement is cautiously framed about the pandemic-driven outlook but strongly supportive on policy (near-zero rates, sustained Treasury and agency MBS purchases, repo/RRP, and reinvestments). The latest SLOOS evidence tempers downside risks in credit transmission: banks reported stronger demand for safer residential mortgage categories—especially GSE-eligible and QM non-jumbo loans, which comprise a large share of bank originations—while demand for subprime mortgages remained weak. At the same time, standards stayed tight and business loan demand was softer, consistent with lingering caution and the role of bank capital positions in lending. Together, this suggests policy support is effectively reaching household mortgage channels, even as riskier segments and business credit remain subdued. Net tone: still slightly negative on the outlook, but marginally improved versus a risk-only read given SLOOS-confirmed strength in core mortgage demand.
